headline: High: Khoj’s broad network egress plus shared-index retrieval can leak or misapply content if paired with externalized email-scheduling workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-python is a static collection with no runtime channel, while Khoj ingests indexed documents and can search them. There is no documented direct bridge, so prompt injection is only plausible if a user manually copies content from the collection into Khoj or indexes it elsewhere.
conditions: IF a user manually copies content from the collection into Khoj’s indexed notes/files
IF Khoj is configured to treat imported text as authoritative instructions
mitigations: Keep the collection out of indexed note sources
Use a separate review-only workspace for pasted content
Add a prefix banner to imported text marking it untrusted
Disable automatic ingestion of arbitrary files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for retrieved snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-python itself has no data classes touched, but Khoj indexes personal notes/files and has broad network egress to APIs/search providers. If the pair shares a workspace or imported files, Khoj can transmit sensitive note contents outward, creating a realistic leakage path in default retrieval workflows.
conditions: IF personal notes or files from Khoj are placed in the same workspace as content derived from the collection
IF Khoj is configured to query external search providers or cloud APIs
mitigations: Restrict Khoj to a local-only backend
Exclude sensitive folders from indexing
Review outbound provider settings before use
Separate public reference material from private notes
requires-engineering: enforce per-source egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write or execution capabilities, while Khoj cannot write files or modify git state. The pair therefore lacks overlapping mutable write surfaces, so direct capability conflict is limited to read-side contention rather than destructive concurrency.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the shared environment
Avoid mounting the same writable directory
Run Khoj with a dedicated index directory
Document any external orchestrator locks
requires-engineering: add resource locking for shared mutable stores

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj’s retrieval/chat flow can treat indexed content as answer material, and awesome-python is a source of reference material that could be copied into that flow. If a user or orchestrator treats retrieved snippets as authoritative, Khoj may propagate errors or stale library recommendations into downstream actions, though no direct action-taking authority is documented.
conditions: IF content from the collection is imported into Khoj’s retrieval corpus
IF downstream users act on Khoj’s answers without independent verification
mitigations: Require human verification before acting on retrieved advice
Mark imported reference text as non-authoritative
Cross-check recommendations against primary sources
Limit Khoj outputs to citations and summaries
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for awesome-python, while Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents and may use cloud or self-hosted APIs. Because the pair lacks evidence of PHI/EU PII handling, compliance risk is limited to policy mismatch if sensitive notes are indexed or sent to external providers.
conditions: IF regulated data is indexed in Khoj
IF Khoj is connected to a non-compliant external API or search provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the index
Use self-hosted providers only
Review retention settings for indexed notes
Separate compliance-sensitive corpora from general notes
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls
